pillar_balance.why: A stock can be strong in some pillars and weak in others; the pillars show where.
pillar_balance.formula: Average of the scores for liabilities to assets and cash conversion (CFO/PAT).

pillar_technical.label: Technical pillar (retired)
pillar_technical.what: A part of the retired overall score, the Technical pillar: the price trend and momentum.
pillar_technical.read: It is no longer shown. Read FinLit Prism and its parts instead.
pillar_technical.why: A stock can be strong in some pillars and weak in others; the pillars show where.
pillar_technical.formula: Average of the scores for price against the 50-day and 200-day averages and the 14-day RSI.

fundamental_score.label: Fundamental score
fundamental_score.what: The fundamental score uses only the business's statements; the technical score uses only the price chart. FinLit never blends the two without showing both.
fundamental_score.read: Long-term investors lean on the fundamental score; the technical score helps with timing.
fundamental_score.why: A great business can have a weak price trend, and the reverse.
fundamental_score.formula: Average of the Quality, Growth, Profitability and Balance sheet pillars (no price trend); needs at least three of the four.

score_change.label: Retired score change since last quarter
score_change.what: How many points the retired overall score moved since the last quarter.
score_change.read: It is no longer shown. Read FinLit Prism instead.
score_change.why: It turns dozens of numbers into one readable starting point.
score_change.formula: The retired overall score now minus the score at the previous quarter, from the stored score history.

strengths_count.label: Strengths found
strengths_count.what: How many strengths FinLit lists for the company.
strengths_count.read: Check the period each finding covers before relying on it.
strengths_count.why: They point to what deserves a closer look.
strengths_count.formula: Number of strengths listed for the company on its report.

watchouts_count.label: Watch-outs found
watchouts_count.what: How many watch-outs FinLit lists for the company.
watchouts_count.read: Check the period each finding covers before relying on it.
watchouts_count.why: They point to what deserves a closer look.
watchouts_count.formula: Number of watch-outs listed for the company on its report.

total_income.label: Total income
total_income.read: Check whether growth comes from selling more or from charging more, and whether it lasts several years.
total_income.why: Growth in revenue is the starting point for growth in profit.
total_income.formula: Revenue from operations plus other income, as reported, in ₹ crore.

other_income.label: Other income
other_income.what: Income that does not come from the main business, such as interest on cash, dividends from investments or gains from selling assets.
other_income.read: If other income is a large share of profit before tax, find out whether it will repeat.
other_income.why: A big jump in other income can make profit look better than the business really is.
other_income.formula: Other income as reported, in ₹ crore.

expenses.label: Expenses
expenses.what: All the costs of running the business: raw materials, staff, rent, power, marketing and so on.
expenses.read: If expenses grow faster than revenue for several quarters, margins are shrinking.
expenses.why: Profit is what is left after expenses, so cost control matters as much as sales.
expenses.formula: Total expenses as reported, in ₹ crore (a bank: interest paid, operating costs and provisions).

operating_profit.label: Operating profit
operating_profit.what: Profit from the core business: revenue minus operating costs, before interest, depreciation, tax and other income. FinLit's P&L shows it this way, which is close to EBITDA.
operating_profit.read: Compare operating profit growth with revenue growth to see whether the business is becoming more or less efficient.
operating_profit.why: It shows how much the business itself earns, separate from how it is financed.
operating_profit.formula: Revenue − operating expenses, where operating expenses exclude finance costs and depreciation. Other income is not included. For a bank: income before provisions.

finance_costs.label: Interest (finance costs)
finance_costs.what: Interest the company paid on its borrowings.
finance_costs.read: Compare it with operating profit to see how comfortably the company pays its interest.
finance_costs.why: Low coverage means a small fall in profit could make interest hard to pay.
finance_costs.formula: Finance costs as reported, in ₹ crore (a bank: interest expended).

depreciation.label: Depreciation
depreciation.what: Spreading the cost of a physical asset, such as a machine, over the years it is used, as a yearly expense.
depreciation.read: A company that buys a lot of equipment will show rising depreciation in the following years.
depreciation.why: It reflects wear and tear and is a real cost, even though no cash leaves in that year.
depreciation.formula: Depreciation and amortisation as reported, in ₹ crore.

exceptional_items.label: Exceptional items
exceptional_items.what: Unusual, one-time gains or losses, such as selling a factory or paying a large fine.
exceptional_items.read: Look at profit both with and without exceptional items before judging a quarter.
exceptional_items.formula: Exceptional items before tax as reported, in ₹ crore.

discontinued_profit.label: Profit from discontinued operations
discontinued_profit.what: Profit or loss from a business the company has sold, closed or demerged.
discontinued_profit.read: A large figure here means reported profit includes something that will not repeat; FinLit's ratios then use the continuing-operations profit.
discontinued_profit.formula: Profit or loss after tax from discontinued operations as reported, in ₹ crore.

profit_before_tax.label: Profit before tax
profit_before_tax.what: Profit after all expenses, interest and depreciation, but before income tax.
profit_before_tax.read: Divide PBT by revenue to get the pre-tax margin.
profit_before_tax.why: It allows comparisons between companies that pay different tax rates.
profit_before_tax.formula: Profit before tax as reported, in ₹ crore.

tax.label: Tax
tax.what: The income tax the company charged to its profit for the year.
tax.read: Indian companies usually pay about 25%; ask why if the rate is far from that.
tax.why: An unusually low rate in one year can flatter profit and make growth from that year look slow later.
tax.formula: Tax expense as reported, in ₹ crore.

net_profit_continuing.label: Net profit from continuing operations
net_profit_continuing.what: Net profit without profit from businesses that were sold, closed or demerged.
net_profit_continuing.read: Check whether net profit is backed by operating cash flow, and whether one-off items inflated it.
net_profit_continuing.why: It is the profit that belongs to shareholders and the base for EPS and P/E.
net_profit_continuing.formula: Net profit minus profit from discontinued operations; shown only when the discontinued profit is material (15% of net profit or more).

diluted_shares_cr.label: Diluted shares (crore)
diluted_shares_cr.what: The number of shares, counting any that could be created, used for earnings per share.
diluted_shares_cr.read: Compare EPS growth with profit growth; if EPS grows slower, new shares are diluting owners.
diluted_shares_cr.why: EPS growth drives share prices over the long run, and it is the 'E' in P/E.
diluted_shares_cr.formula: Diluted number of outstanding shares as reported, in crore.

equity_capital.label: Equity share capital
equity_capital.what: The money shareholders paid in for the face value of their shares.
equity_capital.read: Steady growth in equity alongside low debt is a sign of a sound business.
equity_capital.why: Equity grows when profits are kept in the business and shrinks with losses.
equity_capital.formula: Paid-up share capital on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

reserves.label: Reserves
reserves.what: Profits kept in the business and other reserves, belonging to shareholders.
reserves.read: Retained profit is only useful if the company earns a good return on it; check ROE alongside.
reserves.why: Kept profit funds growth without new borrowing or new shares.
reserves.formula: Reserves and surplus on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

total_equity.label: Total equity
total_equity.what: What would be left for shareholders if the company sold all its assets and paid all its liabilities: the owners' stake. The word also means shares in general.
total_equity.read: Steady growth in equity alongside low debt is a sign of a sound business.
total_equity.why: Equity grows when profits are kept in the business and shrinks with losses.
total_equity.formula: Equity attributable to the company's own shareholders; a bank: share capital plus reserves. In ₹ crore.

minority_interest.label: Minority interest
minority_interest.what: The part of subsidiaries that belongs to outside shareholders, not to this company's own shareholders.
minority_interest.read: Use consolidated figures to judge a group; FinLit labels which one it shows.
minority_interest.why: For groups like Reliance, most of the business sits in subsidiaries, so standalone numbers miss much of the picture.
minority_interest.formula: Non-controlling interest on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

other_liabilities.label: Other liabilities
other_liabilities.what: Everything the company owes other than borrowings.
other_liabilities.read: Compare short-term liabilities with cash and short-term assets to judge whether bills can be met.
other_liabilities.why: Liabilities must be paid, whatever happens to profits.
other_liabilities.formula: Total liabilities minus borrowings, in ₹ crore.

total_liabilities.label: Total liabilities
total_liabilities.what: Money or obligations a company owes to others: loans, unpaid bills, taxes due, customer advances.
total_liabilities.read: Compare short-term liabilities with cash and short-term assets to judge whether bills can be met.
total_liabilities.why: Liabilities must be paid, whatever happens to profits.
total_liabilities.formula: Total liabilities on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore; for a bank: total assets minus equity.

fixed_assets.label: Fixed assets
fixed_assets.what: A long-term physical asset used to run the business, such as land, buildings or machinery, not meant to be sold.
fixed_assets.read: Heavy investment in fixed assets should lead to higher sales in later years; check that it does.
fixed_assets.why: Fixed assets decide how much a company can produce.
fixed_assets.formula: Property, plant and equipment on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

cwip.label: Capital work in progress
cwip.what: Money already spent on assets that are still being built and not yet in use.
cwip.read: Heavy investment in fixed assets should lead to higher sales in later years; check that it does.
cwip.why: Fixed assets decide how much a company can produce.
cwip.formula: Capital work in progress on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

investments.label: Investments
investments.what: Shares, bonds and funds the company holds as investments.
investments.read: Look at the mix: cash is safer than goodwill, and inventory that piles up can be a warning.
investments.why: Assets are what the business uses to earn money.
investments.formula: Current plus non-current investments on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

inventories.label: Inventories
inventories.what: Raw materials, work in progress and finished goods the company holds but has not yet sold.
inventories.read: Rising inventory with flat sales often means demand is weakening.
inventories.why: Inventory ties up cash and can lose value if it goes out of fashion or spoils.
inventories.formula: Inventories on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

receivables.label: Receivables
receivables.what: Money customers owe the company for goods or services already delivered.
receivables.read: If receivables grow much faster than sales, the company may be struggling to collect, or booking sales too early.
receivables.why: Sales are only useful once the cash is collected.
receivables.formula: Current plus non-current trade receivables on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

current_liabilities.label: Current liabilities
current_liabilities.what: Bills and debts the company must pay within a year.
current_liabilities.read: Compare working capital with sales over several years; a sharp rise needs an explanation.
current_liabilities.why: Too little can mean trouble paying bills; too much means cash is stuck in stock and unpaid invoices.
current_liabilities.formula: Current liabilities on the balance sheet, in ₹ crore.

operating.label: Cash from operations
operating.what: Cash generated by the main business in a period, after paying suppliers, staff and taxes.
operating.read: Operating cash flow consistently below net profit needs explaining.
operating.why: It is the clearest sign that a business really earns money.
operating.formula: Cash flow from operating activities in the cash-flow statement, in ₹ crore.

investing.label: Cash from investing
investing.what: Cash spent on or received from long-term assets and investments.
investing.read: A healthy company brings in steady cash from operations, enough to fund its investments over time.
investing.why: Profit can be shaped by accounting choices; cash is much harder to fake.
investing.formula: Cash flow from investing activities in the cash-flow statement, in ₹ crore.

financing.label: Cash from financing
financing.what: Cash raised from or paid to lenders and shareholders.
financing.read: A healthy company brings in steady cash from operations, enough to fund its investments over time.
financing.why: Profit can be shaped by accounting choices; cash is much harder to fake.
financing.formula: Cash flow from financing activities in the cash-flow statement, in ₹ crore.

net_cash_flow.label: Net cash flow
net_cash_flow.what: The total change in the company's cash over the year.
net_cash_flow.read: A healthy company brings in steady cash from operations, enough to fund its investments over time.
net_cash_flow.why: Profit can be shaped by accounting choices; cash is much harder to fake.
net_cash_flow.formula: Net change in cash over the year as reported, in ₹ crore.

capex.label: Capital expenditure
capex.what: Money spent on long-term assets such as factories, machines, stores or networks.
capex.read: Compare capex with operating cash flow: heavy capex funded by debt raises risk.
capex.why: Capex builds future capacity but uses cash today.
capex.formula: Purchase of property, plant, equipment and intangibles in the cash-flow statement (the larger of the two lines), shown as a negative number, in ₹ crore.

free_cash_flow.label: Free cash flow (statement)
free_cash_flow.what: Operating cash flow minus capital expenditure: the spare cash left after keeping and growing the business.
free_cash_flow.read: A company with growing profit but negative FCF for years is consuming cash to grow.
free_cash_flow.why: FCF pays dividends, buybacks and debt repayment.
free_cash_flow.formula: Cash from operations plus capital expenditure (capex is negative), in ₹ crore.

dividends_paid.label: Dividends paid
dividends_paid.what: Cash the company paid out to its shareholders as dividends in the year.
dividends_paid.read: A dividend cut is often a warning about the business; steady increases suggest confidence.
dividends_paid.why: Dividends give a return without selling shares.
dividends_paid.formula: Dividends paid classified under financing activities, in ₹ crore.

revenueYoY.label: Sales growth, year on year
revenueYoY.what: The change in a figure compared with the same period a year earlier, such as Jun 2026 quarter against Jun 2025 quarter.
revenueYoY.read: Use YoY for quarterly results; use QoQ to spot turning points.
revenueYoY.why: It removes seasonal effects, like festive-season sales.
revenueYoY.formula: Quarter sales ÷ sales of the same quarter a year earlier − 1.

revenueQoQ.label: Sales growth, quarter on quarter
revenueQoQ.what: The change in a figure compared with the immediately preceding quarter.
revenueQoQ.read: A strong QoQ jump in a seasonal business may just be the festive quarter.
revenueQoQ.why: It shows the latest direction, but it is affected by seasons.
revenueQoQ.formula: Quarter sales ÷ sales of the quarter before − 1.

operatingProfit.label: Operating profit
operatingProfit.what: Profit from the core business: revenue minus operating costs, before interest, depreciation, tax and other income. FinLit's P&L shows it this way, which is close to EBITDA.
operatingProfit.read: Compare operating profit growth with revenue growth to see whether the business is becoming more or less efficient.
operatingProfit.why: It shows how much the business itself earns, separate from how it is financed.
operatingProfit.formula: Operating profit of the quarter, in ₹ crore.

opYoY.label: Operating profit growth, year on year
opYoY.what: The change in a figure compared with the same period a year earlier, such as Jun 2026 quarter against Jun 2025 quarter.
opYoY.read: Use YoY for quarterly results; use QoQ to spot turning points.
opYoY.why: It removes seasonal effects, like festive-season sales.
opYoY.formula: Quarter operating profit ÷ operating profit of the same quarter a year earlier − 1; withheld when the earlier figure is zero, a loss or missing.

opQoQ.label: Operating profit growth, quarter on quarter
opQoQ.what: The change in a figure compared with the immediately preceding quarter.
opQoQ.read: A strong QoQ jump in a seasonal business may just be the festive quarter.
opQoQ.why: It shows the latest direction, but it is affected by seasons.
opQoQ.formula: Quarter operating profit ÷ operating profit of the quarter before − 1; withheld when the earlier figure is zero, a loss or missing.

netProfit.label: Net profit
netProfit.what: Profit left after every expense, interest and tax: the 'bottom line'. Often called PAT, profit after tax.
netProfit.read: Check whether net profit is backed by operating cash flow, and whether one-off items inflated it.
netProfit.why: It is the profit that belongs to shareholders and the base for EPS and P/E.
netProfit.formula: Net profit of the quarter, in ₹ crore.

profitYoY.label: Profit growth, year on year
profitYoY.what: The change in a figure compared with the same period a year earlier, such as Jun 2026 quarter against Jun 2025 quarter.
profitYoY.read: Use YoY for quarterly results; use QoQ to spot turning points.
profitYoY.why: It removes seasonal effects, like festive-season sales.
profitYoY.formula: Quarter net profit ÷ net profit of the same quarter a year earlier − 1; blank when the earlier profit is zero or a loss.

profitQoQ.label: Profit growth, quarter on quarter
profitQoQ.what: The change in a figure compared with the immediately preceding quarter.
profitQoQ.read: A strong QoQ jump in a seasonal business may just be the festive quarter.
profitQoQ.why: It shows the latest direction, but it is affected by seasons.
profitQoQ.formula: Quarter net profit ÷ net profit of the quarter before − 1; blank when the earlier profit is zero or a loss.

npmChange.label: Net margin change, year on year
npmChange.what: How many percentage points the net margin moved against the same quarter a year ago.
npmChange.read: A net margin of 7.5% means ₹7.50 of profit for every ₹100 of sales.
npmChange.why: It shows how much of each ₹100 of sales the shareholders keep.
npmChange.formula: Net margin now minus net margin a year earlier, in percentage points, worked out from the two growth rates.

gap.label: Gap between sales and profit growth
gap.what: How far apart sales growth and profit growth are for the quarter.
gap.read: A large gap means profit moved much faster or slower than sales, so margins changed a lot.
gap.why: Profit growing faster than sales means margins are widening; slower means they are shrinking.
gap.formula: The absolute difference between year-on-year sales growth and profit growth, in percentage points.

marketCap.label: Market cap
marketCap.what: The total market value of a company: share price multiplied by the number of shares.
marketCap.read: ₹16 lakh crore market cap means the market values the whole company at that amount today.
marketCap.why: It tells you how big the company is in the stock market's eyes and decides whether it is a large, mid or small cap.
marketCap.formula: Share price × shares outstanding, in ₹ crore, as sent with the latest quote.

op_profit.label: Operating profit (annual)
op_profit.what: Profit from the core business: revenue minus operating costs, before interest, depreciation, tax and other income. FinLit's P&L shows it this way, which is close to EBITDA.
op_profit.read: Compare operating profit growth with revenue growth to see whether the business is becoming more or less efficient.
op_profit.why: It shows how much the business itself earns, separate from how it is financed.
op_profit.formula: Operating profit of the latest full year: revenue minus operating costs, before depreciation, interest and other income, in ₹ crore.

op_profit_growth.label: Operating profit growth (annual)
op_profit_growth.what: How much operating profit grew in the latest year.
op_profit_growth.read: Compare operating profit growth with revenue growth to see whether the business is becoming more or less efficient.
op_profit_growth.why: It shows how much the business itself earns, separate from how it is financed.
op_profit_growth.formula: Operating profit this year ÷ operating profit last year − 1; blank when last year was zero or a loss.

op_profit_cagr_3y.label: Operating profit CAGR, 3 years
op_profit_cagr_3y.what: Average yearly growth in operating profit over 3 years.
op_profit_cagr_3y.read: CAGR depends heavily on the start year: growth measured from a bad year looks better than it is.
op_profit_cagr_3y.why: It smooths out ups and downs so different periods and companies can be compared.
op_profit_cagr_3y.formula: (Operating profit now ÷ 3 years ago)^(1 ÷ 3) − 1; blank unless both ends are profits.

op_profit_cagr_5y.label: Operating profit CAGR, 5 years
op_profit_cagr_5y.what: Average yearly growth in operating profit over 5 years.
op_profit_cagr_5y.read: CAGR depends heavily on the start year: growth measured from a bad year looks better than it is.
op_profit_cagr_5y.why: It smooths out ups and downs so different periods and companies can be compared.
op_profit_cagr_5y.formula: (Operating profit now ÷ 5 years ago)^(1 ÷ 5) − 1; blank unless both ends are profits.

vs_ema9.label: Price against 9-day average
vs_ema9.what: How far the price sits above (+) or below (−) its 9-day exponential moving average.
vs_ema9.read: The 9-day average follows the price closely, so this shows short-term stretch.
vs_ema9.why: It describes how far the latest close has moved from its recent path.

vs_ema20.label: Price against 20-day average
vs_ema20.what: How far the price sits above (+) or below (−) its 20-day exponential moving average.
vs_ema20.read: Small gaps mean the price is close to its one-month path.
vs_ema20.why: It shows whether a pullback has reached the one-month average.

ema_stack.label: 9-day above 20-day above 50-day average
ema_stack.what: Yes when the 9-day average is above the 20-day, and the 20-day is above the 50-day.
ema_stack.read: Yes means the shorter averages sit above the longer ones, the pattern of a steady uptrend.
ema_stack.why: It checks that the short, medium and longer paths agree.
ema_stack.formula: 1 if EMA 9 > EMA 20 > EMA 50 on the latest session, else 0.

ema9_hold_10.label: Closes at or above the 9-day average (last 10)
ema9_hold_10.what: Of the last 10 closes, how many were at or above that day's 9-day average.
ema9_hold_10.read: 10 means the price held above its short average every day.
ema9_hold_10.why: It describes how steadily the price has stayed above its short-term path.
ema9_hold_10.formula: Count of the last 10 sessions where close ≥ the 9-day exponential average of that day.

range_10d.label: Range of the last 10 sessions
range_10d.what: The highest high minus the lowest low of the last 10 sessions, as a share of the latest close.
range_10d.read: A small range means the price has moved within a narrow band.
range_10d.why: It shows how tight the recent trading has been.

atr_ratio.label: Volatility now against the longer run
atr_ratio.what: The 10-day average true range divided by the 50-day one.
atr_ratio.read: Under 1 means daily price swings are shrinking against the longer run; over 1 means they are growing.
atr_ratio.why: It compares recent swings with the usual size of swings.

vol_ratio_10_50.label: Volume, last 10 sessions against 50
vol_ratio_10_50.what: The average volume of the last 10 sessions as a multiple of the last 50.
vol_ratio_10_50.read: Under 1 means trading has been quieter than usual; over 1 busier.
vol_ratio_10_50.why: It shows whether trading interest is drying up or building.
vol_ratio_10_50.formula: Mean volume of the last 10 sessions ÷ mean volume of the last 50, from the same daily candles.

vol_ratio_5_50.label: Volume, last 5 sessions against 50
vol_ratio_5_50.what: The average volume of the last 5 sessions as a multiple of the last 50.
vol_ratio_5_50.read: Under 1 means the last week has been quieter than usual.
vol_ratio_5_50.why: It shows the very recent trading activity against the usual.
vol_ratio_5_50.formula: Mean volume of the last 5 sessions ÷ mean volume of the last 50, from the same daily candles.

days_since_high.label: Sessions since the 52-week closing high
days_since_high.what: How many trading sessions ago the highest close of the last 52 weeks was set.
days_since_high.read: 0 means the latest close is the 52-week closing high.
days_since_high.why: It tells how long the price has rested below its high.
days_since_high.formula: Sessions between the latest close and the highest close of the last 252 sessions.

breakout_age.label: Sessions since the latest breakout
breakout_age.what: Sessions since the close last rose above a 52-week closing high that was set at least 15 sessions earlier (last 30 sessions only).
breakout_age.read: Blank means no such breakout in the last 30 sessions.
breakout_age.why: It dates the latest move above an old high.
breakout_age.formula: Latest session t in the last 30 where close > the highest close of the prior 252 sessions and that high is at least 15 sessions old.

breakout_level.label: Level of that breakout
breakout_level.what: The earlier high that the price broke above.
breakout_level.read: The price can come back to this level after a breakout.
breakout_level.why: It names the level that the breakout crossed.
breakout_level.formula: The highest close of the prior 252 sessions on the breakout day.

vs_breakout.label: Price against the breakout level
vs_breakout.what: How far the latest close is above (+) or below (−) the level it broke.
vs_breakout.read: Near 0 means the price has come back to the level.
vs_breakout.why: It shows how far the price has moved from the breakout level since.

breakout_vol_ratio.label: Volume on the breakout day
breakout_vol_ratio.what: The breakout day's volume as a multiple of the 50 sessions before it.
breakout_vol_ratio.read: Above 1.5 means the breakout came on much heavier trading than usual.
breakout_vol_ratio.why: It shows how much trading interest came with the breakout.
breakout_vol_ratio.formula: Breakout-day volume ÷ mean volume of the 50 sessions before it.

b2_age.label: Sessions since the recent breakout
b2_age.what: Sessions since the close rose above a 52-week closing high that was at least 10 sessions old (last 25 sessions only).
b2_age.read: A small number is a fresh breakout; the Breakouts screens look at 3 to 25.
b2_age.why: It shows how long ago the price moved above its old high.
b2_age.formula: Today's session number minus the breakout day's.

b2_level.label: Breakout level, recent 25 sessions
b2_level.what: The earlier 52-week closing high that the price rose above.
b2_level.read: The price now is compared with this level.
b2_level.why: The level is the line the breakout is measured against.
b2_level.formula: Highest close of the 252 sessions before the breakout day.

b2_vs_level.label: Price against the recent breakout level
b2_vs_level.what: How far the latest close is above (+) or below (−) the level it broke.
b2_vs_level.read: Near zero means the price is back at the level.
b2_vs_level.why: It shows whether the old high is holding as a floor.

b2_pullback.label: Below the highest close since the breakout
b2_pullback.what: How far the latest close is below the highest close since the breakout day.
b2_pullback.read: A small positive number is a shallow pullback.
b2_pullback.why: It shows how much of the breakout move has been given back.
b2_pullback.formula: (Highest close since breakout − latest close) ÷ highest close since breakout × 100.

b2_vol_x.label: Breakout-day volume, recent 25 sessions
b2_vol_x.what: The breakout day's volume as a multiple of the 50 sessions before it.
b2_vol_x.read: Above 1.3 means heavier trading than usual on that day.
b2_vol_x.why: It shows how much trading interest came with the breakout.
b2_vol_x.formula: Breakout-day volume ÷ mean volume of the 50 sessions before it.

ema9_above4.label: Last four closes above the 9-day average
ema9_above4.what: Yes if each of the last four closes was above that day's 9-day average.
ema9_above4.why: It shows whether the price is holding close to its short average.
ema9_above4.formula: Each of the last 4 closes > that day's 9-day average.

ema9_near4.label: Last four closes within 4% of the 9-day average
ema9_near4.what: Yes if each of the last four closes was no more than 4% above that day's 9-day average.
ema9_near4.why: It shows whether the price is holding close to its short average.
ema9_near4.formula: Each of the last 4 closes ≤ 1.04 × that day's 9-day average.

ema9_touch4.label: Touched the 9-day average in the last four sessions
ema9_touch4.what: Yes if the low of any of the last four sessions reached the 9-day average.
ema9_touch4.why: It shows whether the price is holding close to its short average.
ema9_touch4.formula: Any of the last 4 lows ≤ that day's 9-day average.

range_4d.label: Range of the last 4 sessions
range_4d.what: The 4-session high minus low, as a share of the latest close.
range_4d.read: A small number is a tight range.
range_4d.why: It shows how quiet the last few sessions were.
range_4d.formula: (Highest high − lowest low of the last 4 sessions) ÷ latest close × 100.

turnover20_cr.label: Average value traded (20 sessions)
turnover20_cr.what: The average of price times volume over the last 20 sessions, in rupee crore.
turnover20_cr.read: A larger number means the stock changes hands more easily.
turnover20_cr.why: It shows how much money trades in the stock on a usual day.
turnover20_cr.formula: Mean of (close × volume) over the last 20 sessions ÷ 1 crore.

prism_final.label: Prism score
prism_final.what: FinLit Prism's rating of the company, 0 to 100, with its rating word (Strong, Healthy, Average, Weak or Poor).
prism_final.read: Higher is better. Read its four parts to see where the rating comes from. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_final.why: One number for the company's financial health: FinLit's only company score.
prism_final.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_fundamental.label: Prism Growth & Profitability
prism_fundamental.what: Prism's Growth & Profitability part, 0 to 100: how steadily sales and profit grow.
prism_fundamental.read: Higher is better. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_fundamental.why: Steady growth in sales and profit is the base of a company's health.
prism_fundamental.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_valuation.label: Prism Valuation
prism_valuation.what: Prism's Valuation part, 0 to 100: the share price against earnings, book value and the company's own history.
prism_valuation.read: Higher means a more modest price for what the company earns. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_valuation.why: The same business can be priced modestly or richly; this part shows which.
prism_valuation.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_quality.label: Prism Quality
prism_quality.what: Prism's Quality part, 0 to 100: borrowing, interest cover, returns and the cash behind profit.
prism_quality.read: Higher is better. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_quality.why: Financial strength decides how a company weathers a bad year.
prism_quality.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_risk.label: Prism Risk
prism_risk.what: Prism's Risk part, 0 to 100: price swings, the largest fall, trading activity and pledged shares.
prism_risk.read: A higher Risk score means lower risk. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_risk.why: Two companies with the same business can carry very different market risk.
prism_risk.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_st_score.label: Prism short-term view
prism_st_score.what: Prism's short-term price trend, from -100 to +100, over weeks.
prism_st_score.read: Above zero the trend is up, below zero down. It describes past prices only. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_st_score.why: It shows how the price has behaved lately, beside the financial picture.
prism_st_score.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.

prism_lt_score.label: Prism long-term view
prism_lt_score.what: Prism's long-term price trend, from -100 to +100, over months.
prism_lt_score.read: Above zero the trend is up, below zero down. It describes past prices only. It describes the company; it is not advice to buy, sell or hold.
prism_lt_score.why: It shows the price's longer direction, beside the financial picture.
prism_lt_score.formula: Worked out by FinLit Prism from the company's filed statements and prices. The model's cut-offs and weights stay with the model.
